title: 353. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Angles in the Same Circle Segment
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Equal Angles in the Same Segment
questions.learningObjective: Identify the relationship between inscribed angles subtending the same chord in the same segment.
questions.question: Which statement is true about two inscribed angles that subtend the same chord and lie in the same segment of a circle?
questions.explanation: Inscribed angles that subtend the same chord from the same segment of a circle intercept the same arc. By the inscribed angle theorem, they are equal. Therefore, the correct statement is that they are equal.
questions.hint: Recall the property of angles in the same segment of a circle.

questions.concept: Applying Equal Angles in the Same Segment
questions.learningObjective: Find an inscribed angle using the equal angles in the same segment property.
questions.question: Distinct points named in this question lie on one circle. In that circle, \(\angle ABC=35^\circ\). Point \(D\) lies in the same segment as \(B\), and \(\angle ADC\) subtends the same chord \(AC\). What is \(\angle ADC\)?
questions.explanation:
Angles in the same segment subtending the same chord are equal. Since \(\angle ABC\) and \(\angle ADC\) subtend chord \(AC\) from the same segment, we have
\[
\angle ADC=\angle ABC=35^\circ.
\]
questions.hint: Use the fact that angles in the same segment are equal.

questions.concept: Equal Angles in the Same Segment
questions.learningObjective: Combine same-segment angles with the triangle angle sum.
questions.question: Distinct points \(A,B,C,D\) lie on a circle, with \(B,D\) on the same arc determined by chord \(AC\). If \(\angle ABC=40^\circ\) and \(\angle DAC=25^\circ\), what is \(\angle ACD\)?
questions.explanation: Angles in the same segment give \(\angle ADC=40^\circ\). In triangle \(ACD\), \(\angle ACD=180^\circ-40^\circ-25^\circ=115^\circ\). Thus A is correct.
questions.hint: Transfer the known inscribed angle to triangle ACD, then use its angle sum.

questions.concept: Equal Angles in the Same Segment
questions.learningObjective: Calculate an inscribed angle in the same segment.
questions.question: Distinct points named in this question lie on one circle. In that circle, \(\angle ABC=48^\circ\). Points \(B\) and \(D\) lie in the same segment, and \(\angle ADC\) subtends the same chord \(AC\). What is \(\angle ADC\)?
questions.explanation:
Because \(B\) and \(D\) lie in the same segment subtending chord \(AC\), the inscribed angles \(\angle ABC\) and \(\angle ADC\) are equal. Thus,
\[
\angle ADC=48^\circ.
\]
questions.hint: Use the equal angles in the same segment property directly.

questions.concept: Equal Angles in the Same Segment
questions.learningObjective: Determine an inscribed angle from another angle in the same segment.
questions.question: Distinct points named in this question lie on one circle. In that circle, \(\angle PQR=62^\circ\). Points \(Q\) and \(S\) lie in the same segment, and \(\angle PSR\) subtends the same chord \(PR\). What is \(\angle PSR\)?
questions.explanation:
Angles in the same segment subtending the same chord are equal. Since \(\angle PQR\) and \(\angle PSR\) both subtend chord \(PR\) from the same segment,
\[
\angle PSR=62^\circ.
\]
questions.hint: Recall that angles in the same segment are equal.

questions.concept: Condition for Equal Angles in the Same Segment
questions.learningObjective: Identify when two inscribed angles subtending the same chord are equal.
questions.question: In a circle, two inscribed angles subtend the same non-diameter chord \(AB\). Under which condition are the two angles equal?

options.label: A
options.text: Their vertices lie on opposite arcs determined by chord \(AB\).

options.label: B
options.text: Their vertices lie on the same arc determined by chord \(AB\).

questions.explanation: Inscribed angles subtending the same chord are equal when their vertices lie in the same segment, that is, on the same arc determined by the chord. For a non-diameter chord, opposite-arc angles are supplementary and unequal. Therefore, the correct condition is that the vertices lie on the same arc.
questions.hint: Distinguish between the same segment and opposite segments.

questions.concept: Converse of the Angle in a Semicircle Theorem
questions.learningObjective: Infer a diameter from an inscribed right angle and calculate the radius.
questions.question: Triangle \(ABC\) is inscribed in a circle. If \(\angle ACB=90^\circ\) and \(AB=10\), what is the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation: An inscribed right angle intercepts a semicircle, so its opposite side \(AB\) is a diameter. Hence the radius is \(AB/2=10/2=5\). Option B is the diameter, not the radius.
questions.hint: Use the converse of the angle-in-a-semicircle theorem, then relate a diameter to a radius.

questions.concept: Solving for a Variable in the Same Segment
questions.learningObjective: Solve for an unknown using the equal angles in the same segment property.
questions.question: In a circle, \(\angle ABC\) and \(\angle ADC\) are inscribed angles in the same segment subtending chord \(AC\). If \(\angle ABC=3x\) and \(\angle ADC=75^\circ\), what is \(x\)?
questions.explanation:
Angles in the same segment are equal, so
\[
3x=75^\circ.
\]
Dividing both sides by \(3\) gives \(x=25\).
questions.hint: Set the two angle expressions equal, then solve for \(x\).

questions.learningObjective: Calculate an inscribed angle in the opposite segment of the same chord.
questions.question: In a circle, chord \(AC\) subtends \(\angle ABC\) and \(\angle ADC\). Points \(B\) and \(D\) lie on opposite arcs determined by chord \(AC\). If \(\angle ABC=110^\circ\), what is \(\angle ADC\)?
questions.explanation:
Inscribed angles subtending the same chord from opposite segments are supplementary. Therefore,
\[
\angle ADC=180^\circ-110^\circ=70^\circ.
\]
questions.hint: Use the supplementary relationship for angles in opposite segments.

questions.concept: Solving for a Variable in the Same Segment
questions.learningObjective: Solve an equation from equal inscribed angles in the same segment.
questions.question: Distinct points \(A,B,C,D\) lie on one circle. In that circle, \(\angle ABC\) and \(\angle ADC\) subtend the same chord \(AC\) and lie in the same segment. If \(\angle ABC=(4x+10)^\circ\) and \(\angle ADC=(2x+50)^\circ\), what is \(x\)?
questions.explanation:
Angles in the same segment are equal, so
\[
4x+10=2x+50.
\]
Subtracting \(2x\) from both sides gives \(2x+10=50\). Subtracting \(10\) gives \(2x=40\), so \(x=20\).
questions.hint: Set the two angle expressions equal, then solve the resulting equation.
